Subject: Renewal planning — smoothing for upcoming surge / temporary price protection

Thanks Logan — quick note from procurement and engineering. Our Q4 roadmap is shifting large parts of inference volume to Redwood for a pilot that could spike usage 2–3x for 2–3 months. Before we commit to an expanded baseline, procurement asked whether Redwood can: 

- provide a short-term price hold (60–90 days) on current committed rates while we stabilize traffic,
- offer a credit mechanism that covers the first-month overage during the surge so we don’t get hit with a single large overage invoice, and
- propose a commit smoothing path so we can amortize a larger annual commit over a flexible schedule.

Can you send a draft term sheet or example language the legal/procurement team can review? Ideally we’d have something to circulate by early next week.

Thanks,
Eleanor Park

Subject: Re: Renewal planning — smoothing for upcoming surge / temporary price protection

Eleanor — really appreciate the context. Attached is a draft term sheet that outlines a pragmatic path we’ve used with other customers facing similar surge-first adoption. High level summary here and then the attached has contract language: 

- Conditional retainer (3–6 month smoothing): a monthly reserved capacity credit that smooths an agreed annual commit across an initial 6-month ramp window. The retainer converts to committed volume on month 7 unless either party elects the 30-day re-eval clause.
- Temporary price hold: we can lock current committed unit pricing for up to 90 days on the baseline committed portion while you ramp. The hold applies only to the baseline units in the retainer; usage above that during the hold is billed at prevailing overage rates but is eligible for a surge credit (see below).
- Surge first-month credit: for any month where usage exceeds 150% of baseline, we will issue a one-time invoice credit equal to the net overage charges above 150%, capped at 25% of that month’s overage value. Credit is applied against the following month’s invoice.
- Upsell ladder: if monthly sustained usage exceeds 1.5x baseline for 3 consecutive months, you automatically qualify for a stepped discount on newly committed volume (documented in term sheet).

Attachments: Renewal term sheet + Q2 usage export (so you can see how the smoothing would have worked historically). A few asks: can procurement confirm the internal approver for a 6-month retainer and whether Helix prefers a 6-month vs 3-month smoothing window? If useful, happy to set a 30-minute call with Marissa (CS) and Karthik (pricing) to walk the doc.

If you want me to redact anything for legal review before circulation, say the word and I’ll produce a clean version.

Best,
Logan Wright

Samir/Eleanor — thanks for the questions and the usage summary. Answers below and I’ve attached an updated term sheet that separates commercial bullets up front (first page) with legal-ready language following. Quick answers: 

- Surge credit application: the credit is issued as an invoice-level credit and will appear on the next invoice cycle (we cannot retroactively change an already-closed invoice). We can, however, prioritize an expedited credit on the same billing period in practice for tight month-ends; the term sheet includes SLA language for expedited processing.
- Retainer conversion/true-up: retainer payments are recorded as prepayments. If the retainer converts to committed volume, prepayments net against the new committed invoices; if it does not convert, remaining prepayment is applied as a one-time account credit or refunded per the conversion clause. The attached example math walks through a 6-month conversion scenario.
- Commercial-first term sheet: attached; legal text starts on page 3.

Next steps I propose: 
- If procurement is comfortable with the update, we’ll generate a DocuSign with the commercial summary for now and the full SOW/legal appendix to follow. Link: https://www.docusign.net/helloworld?envelopeId=abc123def456
- Schedule a 30-min review: Tue 2027-08-03 10:00 AM PT / Wed 2027-08-04 18:00 CEST — Marissa (CS) and Karthik (pricing) will join to talk implementation and billing flow. Please tell me which works.

I’ll hold the proposed 90-day price hold window contingent on signing within 14 days of the DocuSign envelope. Happy to tighten any language procurement requests.

Cheers,
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
